Bud is still grieving the loss of his wife, and his sorrow has made him grumpy, short-tempered and withdrawn. Though he cares deeply for his family and holds to strict principles, he clashes constantly with his two adult children, and he is determined to avoid being placed in a nursing home. At Christmas his 10-year-old British granddaughter, Gloria, comes to stay. Curious, energetic and kind, but sometimes disobedient, she is also dealing with the strain in her parents' rocky relationship and her father's frequent absences, and she likes to film whatever interests her on her smartphone and share it online.

When Bud and Gloria discover a mysterious reindeer living near the family home, the two find common ground. Gloria's persistence wins over her reluctant grandfather, and together they follow the trail of the reindeer, the magical Prancer of the title. Their adventure brings them into conflict with a hunter who wants to shoot the animal, while family tensions over money, including the possible sale of a valuable family house, and the motives of Gloria's money-minded uncle Gerald come to a head. Through his bond with Gloria and the reindeer, Bud begins to open up about his grief, and the family's strained relationships move toward reconciliation in time for Christmas, with the story celebrating loyalty to family, caring for animals, valuing people over money and believing in the spirit of the season.

The film was produced with Sky Cinema. It was released on digital platforms and home video in the United States on November 22, 2022. Alistair Lawrence of Common Sense Media described it as a low-stakes, feel-good holiday drama that spins a decent odd-couple story out of a vague premise, crediting the on-screen chemistry between Cromwell and Ewart for keeping a lightweight script watchable, while noting that the family conflicts are resolved too neatly, that the pursuit of Prancer relies heavily on exposition, and that a stronger villain would have helped.
